02 / THESIS PROJECTA MOBILE APP FOR SCIENCE LEARNING
UNDERGRADUATE THESIS · SCIENCE EDUCATION RESEARCH TEAM

Periodic Table
Explorer.

Have you ever wondered why elements are arranged the way they are? Our thesis answers with a mobile app: a guided, 5E-based journey through periods, groups, atomic structure and reactivity — led by Atomy, our mascot.

5E instructional modelReact Native · ExpoSupabaseGamified learning

One lesson,
five stages.

The app follows the 5E instructional model. Each stage unlocks the next and has its own character, so learners always know where they are in the journey.

  1. 01

    Engage

    Spark your curiosity

    A short video asks why elements are arranged the way they are.

  2. 02

    Explore

    Discover the elements

    Tap through all 118 elements, the 7 periods and the 18 groups.

  3. 03

    Explain

    Understand reactivity

    How electron shells and valence electrons shape each element’s place and behavior.

  4. 04

    Elaborate

    Sort the elements

    Classify 10 random elements as metal, metalloid or nonmetal to earn Atoms.

  5. 05

    Evaluate

    Prove your mastery

    Twelve questions across every topic — finish to earn the Explorer badge.

MEET THE TEAM

Science Education
research team.

We are research students committed to making science education more accessible, understandable and enjoyable.

OUR PURPOSE
Help students explore how elements are arranged in the periodic table through interactive digital tools.
OUR VISION
Bridge the learning gap in understanding the 7 periods and 18 groups through atomic structure and chemical properties.

04 / A LITTLE ABOUT MESTILL LEARNING. ALWAYS CURIOUS.

A student of science.
Always a learner.

CURIOSITY IS WHERE IT BEGINS.

Science has always been my way of asking questions about the world. Education is becoming my way of sharing that curiosity.

I'm Jewel B. Octa, a Bachelor of Secondary Education student majoring in Science at the University of Camarines Norte. Through Field Study 1, I've been connecting what I learn in college with the realities of the classroom.

I still remember a Grade 7 science lesson when a teacher's encouragement gave me the confidence to speak up. That experience stays with me: learning is also about feeling safe enough to ask, try, and make mistakes.
